title: Forward Center Mass
claim: Tests whether a three-layer control projection (117 memory objects → 8 capability operators → ≤3 active fronts → RETURN receipts) improves orientation and execution without rewriting federation canon.
known_limits: Operator mappings are heuristic projections, not canonical classifications.
FCM score is a transparent experimental orientation score, not objective priority.
RETURN receipts persist only in the current browser until exported.
Numeric centrality publishes only degree counts; private dependency identities remain private.
summary: Attention projection over the federation: NOW/NEXT/HOLD/DROP, ≤3 live execution tokens, shared RETURN receipt v0.2, with temporal execution delegated to Atlas Dayline and representation ablation delegated to FIELD / PROOF.

current_classification.basis: CURRENT classifies Center Mass as donor material after useful control-surface direction was absorbed elsewhere; preserve the runnable projection without an independent roadmap.
current_classification.provenance_note: Original release state remains contemporaneous provenance; this field records the later lifecycle classification.
